findings.title: Stack native client with a shared strategy runs getJwt in the client-creation request's context and binds users to the wrong identity
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The new guidance ('a module-level strategy is fine') sits next to a caveat that says the request is only 'not visible' on the stack native path; protect-ffi calls getToken through a Channel from the creating context, so a client built inside a request could silently resolve the first user's JWT, and no test covers that path.

findings.title: Frequent JWT rotation multiplies CTS exchanges and a usage-limit refusal locks out every rotating user for 60 s
findings.label: valid
findings.note: Keying on the whole JWT makes every rotation a new /api/authorise exchange, and settle() records UsageLimitExceeded/OrgNotProvisioned as a strategy-wide 60s denial that engine_for returns for every new JWT, as the cited code shows.

findings.title: Stored tokens from earlier releases, mixed-version deploys and shared stores miss the cache
findings.label: valid
findings.note: BoundStore misses unstamped tokens, and older releases still write unstamped tokens while ignoring the field on read, so new instances re-exchange during a mixed-version deploy; the effect is limited to performance.
